profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
authoring_note: Original content informed by the public framework structure and role-profile intent. No Jisc descriptor text is reproduced or closely paraphrased.

framework_structure_informed_by: Jisc BDC six-element structure and role-profile architecture
source_strategy.role_lens: Specialised profile for digitally enabled service design, administration and support.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, keeps essential digital tasks moving but still relies on prompts, familiar routines or local help when work becomes less predictable.
observable_practices: Uses enterprise systems for routine service delivery and administration when a known example or clear instructions are available.
Keeps case or records workflows moving with some structure, but consistency drops when the task becomes unfamiliar or time-pressured.
Can recover from minor issues in shared service dashboards through search, help or local support, although interruptions still slow progress.
evidence_examples: Examples showing routine use of enterprise systems for predictable tasks.
A simple file, checklist or message trail in case or records workflows that shows work can be completed, albeit with some friction.
A support request, self-note or reflection describing how an issue in shared service dashboards was resolved.

common_misconceptions.claim: Owning or accessing many apps means the basics are secure.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Breadth of access can hide fragile workflow habits and version confusion.

common_misconceptions.claim: Getting through the task once shows the process is reliable.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: One-off success does not show independent, repeatable practice.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, uses core tools independently, chooses sensible workflows and solves common issues without much interruption.
observable_practices: Uses enterprise systems independently and chooses sensible settings or features for the job rather than relying on default habits.
Organises case or records workflows so that current materials, deadlines and permissions are easier for other people to follow.
Troubleshoots common problems in shared service dashboards and makes practical choices that reduce avoidable friction.
evidence_examples: A clean, consistently used setup in enterprise systems that other people can navigate without extra explanation.
A short process note, template or annotated example from case or records workflows showing independent workflow choices.
A troubleshooting example from shared service dashboards where the person diagnosed and fixed a common problem.

common_misconceptions.claim: Being quick personally is the same as having a good workflow.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: A strong personal workaround may still be opaque or awkward for others.

common_misconceptions.claim: A preferred tool is automatically the right choice everywhere.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Fit depends on context, interoperability, support and inclusion.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, optimises workflows, judges tool choices critically and improves practice for other people as well as for themselves.
observable_practices: Improves enterprise systems so that reliability, accessibility or efficiency increase for a wider group, not just for personal use.
Reviews case or records workflows critically, removing duplication and simplifying the workflow where needed.
Makes well-judged decisions about shared service dashboards with attention to interoperability, support burden, inclusion and risk.
evidence_examples: A redesigned or simplified approach to enterprise systems adopted by others or endorsed locally.
Before-and-after evidence from case or records workflows showing improved reliability, accessibility or efficiency.
A comparison or rationale for choices in shared service dashboards that weighs fit, risk, support and interoperability.

common_misconceptions.claim: Proficiency means always adopting the newest or most advanced platform.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Judgment and simplification often matter more than feature depth.

common_misconceptions.claim: If a process works for experts it should work for everyone.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Sustainable improvement must account for different users, needs and support conditions.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, adapts existing materials or familiar methods to meet immediate needs, but design choices are still mostly guided by examples rather than by clear intent.
observable_practices: Adapts existing service guides and forms for immediate use, but most choices still follow familiar patterns rather than an explicit design rationale.
Uses process redesigns to solve a local problem once the route is reasonably clear.
Experiments with templates or automations in a limited way, though evaluation is still mainly about whether something worked at all.
evidence_examples: An adapted version of service guides and forms based on an existing model.
A local workaround using process redesigns that addresses an immediate need.
A brief note on what was changed in templates or automations, even if evaluation is still limited.

common_misconceptions.claim: Changing the look of something counts as innovation.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Surface polish does not by itself improve fitness for purpose.

common_misconceptions.claim: Trying a new tool is enough evidence of creative capability.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Capability lies in the problem solved and the design decisions made.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, creates purposeful outputs or workflow changes that fit the user need, the task and the context.
observable_practices: Designs service guides and forms around the need, the users and the context rather than around the tool alone.
Uses process redesigns to remove repeated effort or improve clarity, consistency or accessibility.
Tests and refines templates or automations enough to show that the change is genuinely useful.
evidence_examples: A purposeful design in service guides and forms with visible choices about structure, format or accessibility.
Evidence that process redesigns reduced repeated effort or improved the user experience.
Feedback or review notes showing that templates or automations was refined after real use.

common_misconceptions.claim: A useful one-off output is automatically reusable.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Reusability usually needs documentation, testing and adaptation for others.

common_misconceptions.claim: More interactivity always means better design.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Good design serves the need; extra features can add friction.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, designs reusable, evaluative and innovative solutions that improve practice beyond the immediate task.
observable_practices: Creates service guides and forms that other people can reuse, adapt or scale with minimal extra explanation.
Treats process redesigns as part of an improvement cycle, with feedback and evidence informing later iterations.
Uses templates or automations to support original, well-scoped innovation rather than novelty for its own sake.
evidence_examples: A reusable package, toolkit or documented pattern built from service guides and forms.
Evidence from process redesigns showing evaluation, iteration and decisions about scale or adaptation.
A short account of how templates or automations changed practice beyond the immediate task.

common_misconceptions.claim: Innovation means large-scale disruption every time.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Many proficient innovations are focused, evidence-led and appropriately scoped.

common_misconceptions.claim: Once a digital solution works, evaluation can stop.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Proficient practice keeps learning from use, context change and feedback.

entries.profile_name: Jisc Building Digital Capability Professional Services Profile
entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, learns reactively when a new need appears and often stops once the immediate task is complete.
observable_practices: Uses role-based guidance when a new need arises, but development activity is still mostly reactive and short-term.
Tries out ideas from service improvement pilots in isolated moments without always checking what changed in practice.
Joins team knowledge sharing when prompted or when confidence is low, though follow-through may be limited once the pressure passes.
evidence_examples: Completion of role-based guidance linked to an immediate need.

common_misconceptions.claim: Watching training content is the same as improving practice.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Development is visible only when learning is applied and reflected on.

common_misconceptions.claim: Only formal courses count as digital development.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Practice, peer exchange and experimentation also matter.

common_misconceptions.claim: Attendance proves that development has happened.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Proficient development looks for transfer into real practice.

entries.capability_statement: In the context of a professional services colleague delivering reliable support, administration or specialist services, finds usable sources or data for immediate tasks, but evaluation of quality, limitations and relevance is still inconsistent.
observable_practices: Uses operational reports or KPIs to locate material for immediate tasks, but source quality checks are still inconsistent.
Reads policy and compliance sources with some care, though assumptions, gaps or definitions can still be missed.
Draws on case or service data to support decisions, but confidence is sometimes based more on convenience than on evidence strength.

A worked example using policy and compliance sources with some attention to meaning, though not all assumptions are checked.
A note or draft using case or service data that shows a plausible but still limited evidence base.

common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Presentation and ranking do not guarantee trustworthiness or fit.

common_misconceptions.claim: Numbers speak for themselves.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Data always depends on definitions, omissions, context and interpretation.

Interprets policy and compliance sources with attention to definitions, missing information, timeframe and context.
Uses case or service data to make reasoned judgments and can explain the limits of the evidence.

common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Critical literacy often requires weighing imperfect evidence, not just discarding it.

common_misconceptions.claim: A neat dashboard is automatically decision-ready.
common_misconceptions.why_inaccurate: Visual clarity can conceal weak measures, missing data or poor alignment with the question.
